text:
maria-peopleops: Hey team — quick Q. My partner and I had a baby in Germany on 2026-02-05 and we just returned to the US. Passport is delayed, still waiting on the consular paperwork. Can I add the baby retroactively to our health/dental/vision? What docs are acceptable if the passport/birth cert are slow? any payroll proration I should expect?
aj: Congrats! :tada: I think you have 30 days from birth for a QLE, but tag @noah-benefits to confirm acceptable docs and timing.
benefits-bot: Hi! For newborn QLEs see: https://hr.redwood.example/new-dependents (docs list + upload instructions). Processing target: 5 business days after docs received.
noah-benefits: Congrats and welcome! Short answers: yes, you can add retro to the date of birth if you submit within the 30-day QLE window and provide acceptable proof. Given it's an overseas birth, acceptable proofs (we accept any TWO of the following):
- Consular Report of Birth Abroad (CRBA) OR local government-issued birth certificate (if English or with certified translation)
- Hospital birth record / discharge summary signed by provider
- Official letter from the U.S. embassy/consulate confirming birth registration
- Passport (once available) OR provisional travel document
If you can't get the CRBA quickly, upload the hospital birth record + embassy letter + a short affidavit (we have a template). Those three together are sufficient for initial enrollment. We do require final official birth certificate/CRBA once issued.
maria-peopleops: Great — thanks. Do translations need an apostille? or is a certified translation fine? Also how does the retro premium get handled?
noah-benefits: Certified translation is fine; apostille not required for our enrollment team. For payroll: coverage effective date will be the date of birth when QLE submitted within 30 days. Premiums are adjusted retroactively in the next payroll cycle following processing; you may see a one-time payroll deduction or a small refund, depending on timing. Typical timeline: we process within 5 business days, payroll posts adjustment in the next pay run (so 1–2 cycles).
emily: I had this happen last year — I uploaded the hospital discharge + interim travel doc and it worked. Also note dental/vision enrollment is separate toggles in the portal, so select those if you want them.
maria-peopleops: Perfect — where exactly do I upload? I already tried the HR portal but couldn't find the event type.
noah-benefits: Steps: 1) Go to HR Portal > Benefits > Report a Life Event 2) Select: "Add dependent — qualified life event (newborn)" 3) Enter DOB (2026-02-05) and relationship: child 4) Upload docs (choose multiple files) 5) In the notes box put: "born abroad — awaiting CRBA/passport; uploading hospital + consular letter" If you prefer, open a case and attach files and cc benefits@redwood.example.
--> Example note to paste:
"Newborn QLE. DOB: 2026-02-05. Born in Germany. Uploading hospital discharge + consular registration letter. Final CRBA/passport will be provided when available"
maria-peopleops: Thanks. Anything special for dependents born abroad re: SSN? we don't have one yet.
noah-benefits: SSN is not required to add the dependent initially. You do need to provide SSN within 60 days if you want dependent tax-free coverage for certain plans; otherwise you can still enroll but HR will follow up. If you can't get SSN within 60 days, we'll keep coverage but may re-audit.
maria-peopleops: Awesome — I'll upload hospital + embassy letter now. One last: does adding retro trigger dependents verification documentation request later?
noah-benefits: Possibly — our verification team may request final CRBA or passport once issued. If we get those later, upload to the same case thread so records are complete.
emily: FYI: if you have FSA/HSA contributions, HSA contributions may be prorated differently — ping payroll if you contribute to HSA.
maria-peopleops: Thanks all. Uploading now and I'll tag here when done. Appreciate the speedy help :heart:
aj: Happy to help, congrats again :celebrate:
benefits-bot: Case created: #BEN-78321. Please attach documents here or to the HR portal. Expected process time: 3–7 business days.
